classification.difficultyReason: Identify which included angle produces each diagonal, use supplementary rhombus angles, then combine the diagonal lengths in the area formula; the parts scaffold this routine chain.

content.prompt: A rhombus $PQRS$ has side lengths $8\text{ m}$, and contains an angle of $128^\circ$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the length of the longer diagonal, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
The longer diagonal is opposite the larger included angle, $128^\circ$. Let its length be $d_L$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}d_L^2&=8^2+8^2-2\times8\times8\cos128^\circ\\d_L^2&=128-128\cos128^\circ\\d_L&=\sqrt{128-128\cos128^\circ}\\d_L&\approx14.38\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length of the shorter diagonal, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, so the other included angle is $180^\circ-128^\circ=52^\circ$. Let the shorter diagonal be $d_S$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}d_S^2&=8^2+8^2-2\times8\times8\cos52^\circ\\d_S^2&=128-128\cos52^\circ\\d_S&=\sqrt{128-128\cos52^\circ}\\d_S&\approx7.01\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the area of the rhombus, correct to two decimal places.

answer.worked:
The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals. Use the unrounded diagonal lengths.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area}&=\frac12d_Ld_S\\\text{Area}&=\frac12\sqrt{128-128\cos128^\circ}\sqrt{128-128\cos52^\circ}\\\text{Area}&\approx50.43\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
